I'm a stay at home Uncle for my niece and nephew, cleaning the house for 6 adults. I would gladly trade it for my old warehouse job working 80 hrs a week. But it is not a hard job at all. It's boring. It's frustrating. It's time consuming. It's gross. It's annoyingly unproductive. But it is the easiest and rewarding "job" I've ever had. I like kids so it's fun being around them as they develop. Babies just demand attention and being held, so it's a pain in the ass trying to get anything done. Plus, cleaning up the same messes every god damn day, fills me with murderous rage. The futility of my existence...

In short, any job you can do in your pajamas, half asleep on the floor, is not a difficult job. Plus, fuck anyone who refers to spending time with their kids as a job.

You need to take a long, hard, look at your relationship if you feel bitter IN ANY WAY about her wanting to be a stay at home mom. If you have ANY DOUBT - pump the damn brakes.

You will work outside, she will work at home. She will become bored and isolated - as much as we hate to admit it, working is a form of social interaction. For better or for worse. It gives our mind stimulation, it gives us something to talk about. She will not have that.

Kids are not easy or convenient. She will have them all day with no break.

You will come home, and she will want a break from the kid. You may be tired from work or stressed by bills as you are the sole breadwinner. You don't want to be a dick - you understand the kid can be a handful. But it's not like you were out drinking and playing golf all day - you were busting ass. You mention it and suddenly you are a bad guy - she wasn't sitting on her ass all day, you know. She was keeping up the house - laundry, dishes, THE KID. Things YOU don't do because YOU weren't home. (You were at work, but if you bring that up it makes the fight longer.)

At this time, you are hurt, tired, look around - and you may notice that the house isn't super clean, or dinner isn't done, or you have no clean underwear because only half the laundry was washed. And The Seed will be planted.

The angry little Seed. You feel under appreciated because you work like a dog to pay the bills and then come home. You love her, you love the kid(s), but you're one person and you're fucking beat. You were under the impression that she was staying home to take care of the house and the kid so you wouldn't have to split the house work 50/50 - the bills aren't split 50/50, and you feel like she isn't holding up her end. It will make you angry. It will make you hurt. It will start to make you resent her.

Don't get me wrong, she has a Seed too - bitter little Seed that remembers when she could go out all the time with friends. She might feel 'trapped' in the house because you're always too tired to take her out, too tired to watch the kid, and there isn't enough money to cover the bills, the kid's needs, and let her go out and do social things. She misses her friends who don't come over during the say because they have jobs, and maybe you asked her really nicely not to have friends over in the evenings because you're fucking tired.

Two people who feel like their shit isn't working out can take a break - get their heads straight, work on the game plan, and come back to the table stronger and ready to work shit out.

But now there's a kid.

She could just leave your ass and you can pay child support. She don't need no man - she'll be a strong single woman taking care of her kid, getting the job that could have saved your relationship if she'd been willing to get it earlier. You will feel awful, like you weren't able to make her happy and you can't remember why. You both have reasons to shit talk each other but they're all Non-Reasons - just stupid little Seeds that grew from being too tired and too bored.

Being a stay at home mom can be a wonderful, rewarding thing. Having a spouse that is a stay at home spouse can be wonderful too. But if you don't want that don't pretend you do in order to stay in a relationship. You will get bitter, angry, and then a kid or two suffers for it. If you don't think you can work to support a house alone, be up front about it. It's not being weak, it's being real and if you're talking about getting married and makin' babies you need to get real as fuck. Not trying to scare you, just trying to warn you before a third or fourth life gets involved and robs me in 14 years.

You aren't crazy or a bad person for taking time to think this over, OP. GL.
